question: is the residual non-monotone downforce drift (0.0104 with linearUpwind) dominated by the declared far-field domain or by the far-field boundary treatment?

fixed_conditions.candidate: opt_q100_b0_step0_try0_block (same STL hash as the fixed-domain study)

factors.name: far-field domain size
factors.treatment: extend every far-field face by one body length (0.8 m) while keeping the body, operating point, and mesh resolution at V2

factors.name: far-field boundary treatment
factors.baseline: declared inlet/outlet/symmetry set of the fixed-domain family
factors.treatment: single documented variant (e.g. pressure-outlet on the top face) chosen and recorded before the run

metric.primary: downforce change between the baseline V2 and each treatment V2
metric.secondary: Cd relative change and force stationarity

decision: if a factor moves the V2 downforce by more than the registered bound, register that factor, rerun the family, and repeat the V2->V3 drift measurement; otherwise the residual drift is accepted as a measured candidate-specific band and no further factor is registered
stop_conditions: no V3 runs in this campaign
a treatment that fails mesh/stationarity gates is reported as failed, never dropped
changing the treatment definition after seeing results closes the campaign and requires a new manifest
